answer: Let the anchor be a trusted seed in the attestation graph, and assign voting weight by bounded-length random walks from it. If a sybil cluster containing nodes named walnut and atlas has low conductance—few outgoing attestations relative to its volume—walks cross its sparse cut infrequently. Under bounded degree and walk length, this limits the cluster’s reachable mass and aggregate voting weight; min-cut bounds make the isolation robust to individual edge changes.
